questions.question: Does an 'else' statement have its own condition (e.g. else x < 5:)?
options: No, else catches everything not caught by if and has no condition
Yes, else always requires a condition
questions.correct_answer: No, else catches everything not caught by if and has no condition
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! else never takes a condition; it acts as the default fallback branch.
questions.explanation_incorrect: else has no condition. If you need a second condition, use elif.

questions.question: Can both the 'if' block and 'else' block execute in a single run?
options: No, they are mutually exclusive (only one can run)
Yes, if the number is zero
Yes, if both conditions are True
questions.correct_answer: No, they are mutually exclusive (only one can run)
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! An if/else construct executes exactly one path.
questions.explanation_incorrect: if and else are mutually exclusive: either if runs or else runs, never both.

questions.question: What keyword is used in Python for 'else if' to check multiple conditions in order?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Python uses 'elif' for chained conditional checks.
questions.explanation_incorrect: In Python, the contraction 'elif' is the keyword for else-if.

questions.explanation_correct: Correct! x > 20 is False, but elif x == 10 is True, so 'B' is printed.
questions.explanation_incorrect: The first matching condition (elif x == 10) executes, outputting 'B'.
